content.text:
**Finding: deviation (critical) — § 21.1 cap basis is illusory.**

What the document gets right: the cap is expressly mutual, § 21.2 mutually excludes indirect/consequential damages (and helpfully treats data-restoration, replacement services, notice and incident-response costs as direct damages), and § 21.3 carves out confidentiality, data-protection, security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement as uncapped Excluded Claims, with Customer's payment obligation excluded from "damages."

The defect is quantum. "Fees" is defined at § 1.5 as *only* the Implementation Fee, which § 1.6 fixes at a one-time USD 12,000 under the first Order Form — and § 21.1 compounds this by limiting the basis to the first Order Form. Vendor's total exposure is therefore capped around USD 12,000 no matter the subscription spend, well below the walk-away threshold of six months' fees.

Redline (validated, preferred level) amends only the cap sentence to the greater of (a) all amounts paid or payable by Customer under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the preceding twelve months and (b) USD 1,000,000, preserving the existing mutuality and Excluded Claims architecture.
